# PHP Human Runco: Action Matching, Visual Policy, and MuJoCo Experience

PHP (Perceptive Humanoid Parkour) enables the Unitree G1 to continuously perform actions such as crossing, climbing, bridging, and rolling based on onboard depth perception and direction commands. It is suitable for learning a complete problem: **how to connect multiple dynamic skills together, and enable the robot to choose the appropriate action according to the obstacles in front of it.**

This chapter starts with the browser experience, and then introduces the local operation and training procedures for official pre-trained models. The content is based on the official papers and code compiled on 2026-10-23; this chapter provides an introduction to the methods and official reproduction steps. PHP training or local policy evaluation have not been carried out in this project yet.

## 2. Experience it in the browser first

Open the [ official interaction page ](https://php-parkour.github.io/demo.html), and wait for the model and scene to load. The web page runs a MuJoCo simulation within the browser, making it suitable to observe how the policy responds to direction and speed commands first.

| Webpage button | Function |
| --- | --- |
| `W` | Move forward; hold until landing when crossing obstacles |
| `A` / `D` | Turn left / right |
| `Y` | Switch between high and low speed modes |
| `Space` | Pause |
| `Backspace` or Page Reset button | Reset the round |

It is recommended to first align with a obstacle and maintain `W`, observing the stages of approach, contact, crossing, and landing. After getting familiar with this, perform short manipulation operations to align with the next obstacle. The direction is controlled by humans, while the specific obstacle-crossing actions are executed based on the policy combined with observations. [ manipulation instructions come from ](https://php-parkour.github.io/).

## 3. From Action Segments to Perceptual Policy

The PHP training process consists of three steps: first, generate continuous reference actions; then, train experts that can track these actions in physical simulation; finally, distill the experts into a unified policy using depth maps.

![PHP Official Method Diagram: Action Matching, Teacher Training, and Perceiving Student Policy](https://php-parkour.github.io/static/images/fig2_method.png)

The image comes from the [ official project page ](https://php-parkour.github.io/), and the original labels are retained.

| Phase | Main Inputs | Outputs | Key Learning Points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Motion Matching | Atomic actions, terrain, and motion targets redirected to the robot | Long-term kinematic reference trajectory | Ensure smooth transition between skills in posture and motion trends |
| Teacher Training | Reference trajectory, privileged state, and terrain observations | Reinforcement learning experts for each skill | Track reference actions during contact dynamics |
| Student Training | Depth map, proprioceptive state, and direction commands; supervised by the teacher | Perceivable-driven multi-skill policy | Mimic the teacher’s access state and improve performance through RL |

**Action matching is responsible for “how to connect.”** The paper describes it as nearest neighbor retrieval in the feature space: finding segments from the action library that align with the current state and motion goal to form a continuous trajectory. The reference trajectory is then provided to the reinforcement learning expert for physical execution learning.

**DAgger is responsible for “whether it will continue to perform after deviating”.** The actual state of the student policy during access differs from the teacher demonstration state. Daggerg obtains teacher supervision based on the student access state; combined with RL optimization, a policy capable of executing various skills according to depth perception is formed. For details, see the [ paper, ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15827v2) and [ official code overviews, and ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour).

During deployment, the two models work together: `depth_backbone.onnx` provides the encoding depth map, and `student.onnx` converts visual features, ontology state, and direction commands into joint targets. Therefore, two files exported by the same version are required during runtime. [ model interface description ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/DEPLOY.md).

## 4. Choose a learning path

| Route | Environmental Requirements | Suitable Targets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser Experience | Browsers capable of opening the official demo | Understanding commands and recognizing the relationship between perception and obstacle avoidance behavior |
| Local MuJoCo Inference | Official Holosoma MuJoCo / inference environment and graphical desktop | Running published student policies and observing deep inputs and physical closed loop |
| Action Matching | Conda; this step does not require Isaac Sim | Generating, checking, and combining reference actions |
| Teacher Training and Student Distillation | Linux, NVIDIA GPU, Isaac Sim | Training skill experts and exporting one’s own policy |

The local commands in this chapter follow the official Linux approach. For the hardware stack used in full training, see [ training guide ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/README.md); AMD learners can use the browser entry first to experience it.

## 5. Running the official pre-trained policy locally

### 5.1 Fixed Code and Holosoma Versions

The official code relies on its fixed Holosoma sub-module. The following submission is the version verified in this chapter; the source code and model are placed in an independent directory outside the tutorial repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour.git
cd php_parkour
git checkout c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

All subsequent commands are executed from the `php_parkour` root directory, and the action matching section will clearly switch to the directory.

### 5.2 Prepare the Running Environment and Model

For the first installation, create the MuJoCo and inference environment using the official script; if the environment has already been installed for this version, these two steps can be skipped:

```bash
bash thirdparty/holosoma/scripts/setup_mujoco.sh
bash thirdparty/holosoma/scripts/setup_inference.sh
```

The startup script defaults to using the `hsmujoco` and `hsinference` environments under `~/.holosoma_deps/miniconda3`. If you want to reuse other Holosoma checkout environments, rebind them as an editable installation according to the [ official deployment guide ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/DEPLOY.md).

Use the official resource script to obtain student models:

```bash
python scripts/download_assets.py student
python scripts/download_assets.py student --verify
```

The default directory is `~/.cache/php-parkour/student`. You can use `--destination DIR` to change it to your own model directory. The script verifies the size and SHA-256 of the compressed package and model files according to the repository's `release-assets.json`. `--verify` only checks existing files. The public student package provides two ONNX models. [ download entry and resource description ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour).

### 5.3 Simulate First, Then Reason

Start it in two terminals on the same machine. A graphical desktop is required; when using SSH, configure the `DISPLAY` in both terminals to the same available desktop.

Terminal 1:

```bash
bash ./run_php_sim.sh
```

After seeing that the deep shared memory `depth_img_shm` has been created and its shape is `(1, 1, 58, 87)`, start Terminal 2:

```bash
PHP_STUDENT_DIR="$HOME/.cache/php-parkour/student"
BACKBONE="$PHP_STUDENT_DIR/depth_backbone.onnx" \
STUDENT="$PHP_STUDENT_DIR/student.onnx" \
bash ./run_php_inference.sh
```

The inference side should report that the shared memory with the same name has been connected. Then, in the MuJoCo window, press `8` to lower the hanger so both feet touch the ground, and then press `9` to remove the hanger; on the policy terminal, press `]` to activate the policy. Move forward and backward with `w` / `s`, give a left-right 45° direction with `a` / `d`, a left-right 90° direction with `q` / `e`, and switch the speed with `=`. Press `o` to enter the damping mode, press `i` to return to the starting position, and press `Backspace` in the MuJoCo window to reset the environment.

**The local version differs from the web interface buttons**: The web switching speed is denoted by `Y`, while the local inference endpoint uses `=`. For detailed instructions, see the [ official sim2sim guide ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/DEPLOY.md).

### 5.4 Common Questions

| Phenomenon | Check Location |
| --- | --- |
| Unable to find Holosoma or startup script | Verify that the fixed version of the sub-module has been initialized, and start it from the PHP root directory |
| Warning: Missing model | Pass `BACKBONE` and `STUDENT` simultaneously, and check the actual paths of both files |
| Inference side fails to wait for depth map | Start the simulation first, ensure `depth_img_shm` is created, and both ends have consistent shapes |
| Robot remains suspended | Perform `8` and `9` manipulations in the simulation window, then use `]` in the policy terminal |
| Continues after direction key release or key input is invalid | Check the graphical desktop, window focus, and `DISPLAY` settings for SSH |

During restart, exit the previous PHP simulation and reasoning processes; the simulation launcher will rebuild the deep shared memory.

## 6. From reference actions to your own policy

This section provides the learning order and minimum entry points. After completing local inference, you can first check the action and terrain data, and then proceed with teacher and student training.

### 6.1 Generate and View Reference Actions

Prepare the action matching environment and database in the PHP root directory:

```bash
bash motion_matching/setup_env.sh
conda activate php-motion-matching
python scripts/download_assets.py databases
cd motion_matching
python -m motion_matching.run --mode generate --scenario high_speed_climb_76
python -m motion_matching.motion_visualizer \
  --motion-file motion_matching_results/high_speed_climb_76
```

Open the address provided by the visualization program and check whether the actions and obstacles are aligned, and whether the skill transitions are smooth. The generated results are exported at 50 FPS, including the reference action `*_motion.npz`, obstacle description `*_terrain.npy`, and visual grid `*_terrain.obj`. For methods to generate extended scenarios, see [; for action matching guidelines, see ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/motion_matching/README.md).

### 6.2 Training the teacher using official example data

Returns to the PHP root directory from the action matching directory. The official source provides five sets of example actions and terrain data: locomotion, low/high speed step, low/high speed climb-76. You can start training directly from the teacher mode:

```bash
cd ..
bash wbt_training/training_runs/setup_env.sh
source scripts/source_isaacsim_setup.sh
python scripts/download_assets.py motions-locomotion
wandb login

REGISTRY="file://$HOME/.cache/php-parkour/motions-locomotion" \
NGPUS=1 \
bash wbt_training/training_runs/run_terrain_teacher.sh \
  --training.headless True --training.num-envs 4096 \
  --training.name example-locomotion-teacher
```

Here, the walking teacher is trained; other skills require switching to corresponding data and training separately. The example package is the training data, while the published student ONNX is used for direct inference.

### 6.3 Distillation, Evaluation, and Export

After the teacher training is completed, replace the reference below with the teacher run of your W&B project:

```bash
TEACHER_CHECKPOINT='wandb://your-team/php-experiments/TEACHER_RUN_ID' \
REGISTRY=auto NGPUS=1 FINETUNE=1 \
bash wbt_training/training_runs/run_terrain_warp_distill.sh \
  --training.headless True --training.num-envs 4096 \
  --training.name my-student
```

`FINETUNE=1` is the default DAgger＋PPO approach, while `FINETUNE=0` uses pure DAgger. When there are multiple teachers, the teachers' references are separated by commas; `REGISTRY=auto` restores the datasets of each teacher in order. When only the walking teacher is trained, the student's learning range is limited to walking; to learn crossing and climbing, the corresponding teachers need to be added.

```bash
CHECKPOINT='wandb://your-team/php-experiments/STUDENT_RUN_ID' \
REGISTRY=auto bash wbt_training/training_runs/eval_student.sh
```

When students' training checkpoints are saved, the corresponding ONNX files will be automatically exported. After evaluating the students' performance, the two exported models can be used in the MuJoCo running process described in Section 5. The number of parallel environments is the total across GPUs, adjusted according to memory availability; W&B is used by default for official training and evaluation. When pure local logging is required, `LOGGER=disabled` can be set. For complete configurations and manual export methods, see the [ training guide and ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/README.md), and for the distillation switch, see the [ startup script and ](https://github.com/amazon-far/php_parkour/blob/c7c9ce3fc75a8754a7e403c58de3b6933254d01b/wbt_training/training_runs/run_terrain_warp_distill.sh).

## 7. Learning Records and Related Reads

When learning for the first time, three things should be recorded: what command direction is given, at what distance the robot starts to change its motion, and whether it can continue walking steadily after crossing obstacles. Local experiments should also include the code version, model source, obstacle settings, full round video, and number of successful attempts, so as to facilitate comparison between different models and scenarios.

Next, read the [Booster K1 web page on MuJoCo and AMP training ](../02-BoosterK1-mjlab-AMP/README.md) in the same chapter to compare the training approaches for motion priors and action tracking; you can also read [BeyondRetarget monocular video reproduction ](../03-beyondretarget-monocular-video-action-reproduction/README.md) to understand the connection between generating robot actions from human videos and training physical control strategies.
